decisions.evidence: Maker R2: “quickly save a link”; Maker R4: paste the address, wait for details, then “Save bookmark.” Client R4: “exactly the quick-save I wanted.” Client R23 also confirms a valid address may save without tags.
decisions.note: Conforming URL-save decision, established during goal alignment and prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2’s core summary omits automatic metadata. Client R2 adds: “when I paste a link, the app should pull in the page’s title and description automatically.”
decisions.note: The client restores a related reference requirement missing from the goal summary. The correction covers title and description, not the reference item’s full metadata set.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2’s proposed core omits duplicate handling. Client R2 adds: “if I happen to paste a link I’ve already saved, I’d rather it take me to edit the existing one than end up with duplicates.”
decisions.note: Corrective extension during goal alignment: the client supplies the omitted duplicate-save rule.

decisions.evidence: Maker R5 presents tag entry before saving; Client R5 approves the tag-chip interaction. Maker R6 presents saving with both “web design” and “reference”; Client R6 confirms both tags appear.
decisions.note: The tag-assignment decision conforms, including multiple tags.

decisions.evidence: Maker R9 presents clicking the “web design” tag to show only bookmarks with that exact tag and a clear-filter control. Client R9: “This is the tag-filtering I wanted.”
decisions.note: Conforming exact-tag filtering decision at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker R12 presents the bookmark title as a link to the original URL, opening in a new tab. Client R12 confirms it opens “the real MDN page” in one click.
decisions.note: Conforming navigation decision; opening a new tab is an additional compatible choice.

decisions.evidence: Maker R14 presents confirmed deletion that removes the bookmark from the list. Client R14: “only after I pressed ‘Delete bookmark’ did it actually remove the card.”
decisions.note: Conforming deletion decision; confirmation is an additional safety behavior.

decisions.evidence: Client R1 expresses the expectation: “saving a note on a link.” Maker R2 presents “Notes … can wait for a later cycle”; Client R2 explicitly accepts: “I’m happy to leave notes … for later.” Maker/Client R25 and R26 reaffirm that deferral.
decisions.note: The client explicitly identifies the expected note feature and accepts its deferral. This is one continuing scope decision, not three repeated counts.

decisions.evidence: Client R1 asks for “keeping a saved copy of the page in case it disappears.” Maker R2 presents “offline copies … can wait”; Client R2 explicitly accepts leaving “offline copies” for later. R25–R26 reaffirm the same deferral.
decisions.note: Explicitly accepted departure from local page preservation during scope formation; later gate and implementation statements reaffirm rather than revise it.

decisions.evidence: Client R1 expects “tidying up old ones by archiving instead of deleting.” Maker R2 says archiving can wait; Client R2 explicitly accepts leaving “archiving for later.” Client R26 again says archiving remains for a future round.
decisions.note: The client states both the archive expectation and its distinction from deletion, then knowingly accepts deferral. No separate archived-list behavior was presented, so REF-BM-28 is not inferred.

decisions.evidence: Maker R4 specifies that “the title and description” appear automatically; Client R4 confirms those fields and later summaries refer only generally to “automatic page details.” The record never states whether favicon and preview image are also collected.
decisions.note: After the R2 correction, the revised metadata presentation is incomplete relative to the full reference item. Absence of favicon/preview collection cannot be established from silence, so divergence remains unresolved.

decisions.evidence: Client R4 reports the resulting list shows “the title, description, and site”; R6 confirms tags appear, and R7 retains the same list layout. Neither presentation nor response establishes whether a favicon is exposed per item.
decisions.note: The recorded list presentation covers several required fields, but the evidence cannot establish full conformity or divergence for the favicon requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker R5 presents version 1 as type-and-Enter chips, with the existing tag only demonstrating display. Client R5 says: “I’d like it to suggest tags I’ve already used” and requests that behavior be added to version 1.
decisions.note: Corrective extension during prototype review: the chosen interaction initially lacks the required existing-tag autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Maker R6 presents the revised interaction where typing `ref` shows the existing `reference` suggestion and Enter reuses it. Client R6: “That’s exactly what I wanted.”
decisions.note: The revised autocomplete decision conforms and is distinct from the earlier corrected presentation.

decisions.evidence: Maker R7 frames the behavior as “title-and-description search”; Maker R25 later summarizes search across “titles, descriptions, and tags,” while notes remain explicitly deferred. Client R7 approves only the title/description behavior, and Client R25 gives general scope approval without surfacing the missing note-search dimension.
decisions.note: The settled search scope cannot search bookmark notes because notes were explicitly excluded, so it diverges from full-text search over title, description, note, and URL. The client does not identify this difference in the search response.

decisions.evidence: Maker R8 instructs the client to type bare `web design`, which matches bookmarks through tags. Client R8 approves bare-text tag matching. The record never tests or states whether `#tag` syntax is supported or rejected.
decisions.note: Bare-text tag matching could coexist with the required `#tag` syntax; the evidence therefore establishes neither divergence nor conformity.

decisions.evidence: Maker R10 presents a one-click star that adds a bookmark to Read later. Client R10 chooses it and confirms the “Added to Read later” result.
decisions.note: Functionally conforming decision to mark a bookmark unread/read-later.

decisions.evidence: Maker R11 presents a dedicated Read later list showing only marked items. Client R11: “Having one clear place to go back to the things I flagged for later is exactly what I wanted.”
decisions.note: Conforming separate unread-bookmark view.

decisions.evidence: Maker R13 enumerates editable fields as “address, title, description, and tags,” with notes already deferred. Client R13 repeats that those four fields are editable and calls it “exactly” right, without mentioning the missing note field.
decisions.note: The concrete edit-form decision omits bookmark notes and therefore diverges from REF-BM-04. The response does not surface that difference at this review.

decisions.evidence: Maker R15 presents immediate recognition of an already-saved URL and opening its populated edit form without another copy. Client R15 confirms it is “exactly what I wanted.”
decisions.note: The revised duplicate-save presentation conforms after the earlier corrective request.

decisions.evidence: Maker R4 presents fetched title and description for preview before saving; Maker R13 establishes post-save editing; Maker R17 permits manual title/description entry after a fetch failure. No entry establishes whether successfully auto-collected title/description can be edited before saving.
decisions.note: Post-save editing is shown, but the required pre-save editing of successfully collected metadata remains indeterminate.

decisions.evidence: Maker R20 presents clicking the filled star so the item leaves the Read later list without deleting the bookmark. Client R20 explicitly interprets this as “marking something as read” and approves the distinction.
decisions.note: Functionally conforming mark-read behavior.
